letters.title: On Your Worst Days
letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
You think I fell for the version of you
that arrives on time with her hair done.

I did not.

I fell for the one who cries at adverts,
who goes quiet for two days and calls it nothing,
who eats standing up over the sink at midnight
because sitting down would make it a meal.

Come to me undone. That is not the exception
I am generously willing to allow.
That is the whole invitation.

letters.title: Take the Time
letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
There is no clock in this.

Take the evening. Take the week.
Take the year, if the year is what it needs,
and do not spend any of it apologising to me.

I am not keeping a tally,
and there will be no invoice at the end,
no quiet accounting of what your silence cost me,
handed over later when I want something.

I would rather wait for you badly
than be handed something you were hurried into.

letters.title: Between
letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
If something is coming for you
it will have to come through me first.
That part was easy. I decided that early
and I have not thought about it since.

The harder promise is the other one.

That I will never stand between you
and the thing you have decided you want,
even when the thing you want
is a little further away from me.

Go. I will be the wall at your back.
Never the one in front of you.

letters.title: What I See
letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
I will not get used to you.

That is the promise, and it is harder than it sounds,
because getting used to people is the thing people do.
It is how the miraculous becomes furniture.

So I will keep looking at you properly.
And when I see something,
I will say it out loud, including the difficult ones,
even when the room would be easier if I did not.

You did not ask for someone comfortable.
You asked for someone who is paying attention.

letters.title: Beside, Not After
letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
Not behind me.
Not after me on the invitation, in smaller letters.

Beside.

Whatever I build, your name sits on it
at exactly the same height as mine,
and if there is ever only room for one of us
in the doorway, the lift, the last seat on the train,
it is you. There is no version where I have to think about it.

I have never wanted to be the story.
I want to be the other half of one.

letters.title: Carried
letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
If the worst ever comes, I will not put you down.

I want that in writing now, while it is still hypothetical
and easy to say and costs me nothing.

I would not build a shrine.
I would carry you the ordinary way.
In how I make tea. In the songs I skip.
In the way I would still say we
long after there was any reason to.

Not as grief.
As something I wear.
